html:
La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia, in a deep canyon at about 3,600 metres above sea level. The Spanish founded it on 20 October 1548 as a stop on the road between Potosí and Lima.

It grew as a market for the Aymara farmers of the Altiplano and a trading town on the silver route. In 1781 the rebels of Túpac Katari besieged it for months. After the civil war of 1899, the government moved there from Sucre, which remains the official capital.

The city spills up the canyon walls to the plateau above, where El Alto has grown into a separate city of mostly Aymara migrants. Its cable cars, opened from 2014, form the largest urban cable car network in the world. It is the political centre of Bolivia and the site of the protests of the gas war.
